$comment: Production health model. CORE decides overall readiness; SOURCE health is per-source and never gates release.

core.pass: HTTP 200 and level READY or DEGRADED (never BLOCKED / 503); degraded reasons are listed, secret values never returned

core.probe: GET {ccos}/ready (READY/DEGRADED/BLOCKED; D1, required schema, operator auth, handoff + callback config, bindings) and GET {ccos}/version (commit, deployedAt, contractVersion, expectedSchema)
core.pass: HTTP 200 and level READY or DEGRADED (never BLOCKED / 503); degraded reasons are listed, secret values never returned

core.probe: python adapters/tip-toplulugu-radar/scripts/tip_toplulugu_ops.py status + capacity; GCOS /api/ready CRON_HEARTBEAT_STALE absent
core.pass: capacity guard not BLOCK; no source lateness > 2880 min; no CAPACITY_DELAY in last run report

core.probe: GCOS /api/system-health (D1 read) and CCOS probe above (D1 read)
GCOS /api/ready has no STATUS_CALLBACK_TOKEN_NOT_CONFIGURED; CCOS GET /ops/summary intake.callbacks (failed, exhausted) and signals
core.pass: no undelivered callbacks older than one retry window; recover with CCOS POST /ops/callbacks/redeliver

source.rule: Individual source health (feed failures, disabled/pending/manual sources, R4 research, curated-club, backlog) is reported per source and NEVER affects core readiness or release.
